title: Frontend: shuffle()
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind shuffle(). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({values,draws}). Apply Fisher–Yates to a copy, consuming one supplied draw in [0,1) for each index from length-1 down to 1. Return the permutation. Draw count is sufficient.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Copy the input, then for each position from the end choose a uniform integer between zero and that position inclusive and swap.
alternativeApproaches: Use rejection-sampled cryptographic integers for a stronger randomness requirement and explain why distribution tests are not a proof.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty/single item; unchanged input; deterministic swaps.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
